objective: Sub-goal B191, the coordinator's go-ahead 2026-11-17 for direction A gated by D (goals G15, G16). D: do pairs of distinctions whose relative value the fast loop (Novelty+) keeps fixed while both flip predict provable ties (local window 10) and the planted relative values (random patterns) better than random co-knotted pairs? A: merge such pairs speculatively, without proof, at their current relative value, let the search run on the coarser pattern, and undo the latest merges when it stalls; these moves do not keep the allowed states, and every reported state is checked on the original knots. Random patterns are primary (where proof-based moves found nothing), local window 10 for contrast; tuned Novelty+, five runs, fresh instances, corrected charge and whole-run CPU; control: the same schedule merging random co-knotted pairs. Publication hold: a general speed-up on random patterns at scale is reported to the coordinator before any commit.
title: Do speculative merges chosen from a fast search's own co-flip evidence, undone when the search stalls, cut the charged work of solving planted knot patterns where provable moves find nothing?
